name.text: Finding exponetial functions of given points

questiontext.text:
Find the exponentail function of the form \( f(x)=Ca^x\) whose graph passes through the points \(({@x1@},{@y1@})\) and \(({@x2@},{@y2@})\) as shown below

[[jsxgraph]] var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-10, {#y2*1.1#}, 10, -5], keepaspectratio: false, showCopyright: false, axis: true, showNavigation:false }); // Define points var point1 = board.create('point', [{#x1#}, {#y1#}], { name: '\\(({#x1#}, {#y1#})\\)', color: 'red', size: 4, fixed: true }); var point2 = board.create('point', [{#x2#}, {#y2#}], { name: '\\(({#x2#}, {#y2#})\\)', color: 'red', size: 4, fixed: true }); // Define function function f(x) { return {#cor_c1#} * Math.pow({#cor_a1#}, x); } // 3*2^x is C*a^x where C=3 and a=2 // Plot function curve var curve = board.create('functiongraph', [f, -10, 4], { strokeColor: 'blue', strokeWidth: 2, fixed: true }); [[/jsxgraph]]

generalfeedback.text:
Worked Solution

\(f(x)=Ca^{x}\)

At \(({@x1@},{@y1@})\) we get \({@eq1@} \implies \displaystyle a={@fx11@}\)

At \(({@x2@},{@y2@})\) we get \({@eq2@}\)

Substitute \(\displaystyle a={@fx11@} \) into \(\displaystyle {@eq2@}\) and Solve for \(C\)

\(\displaystyle \begin{aligned} {@y2@} &= C \left( {@fx11@} \right)^3 \\ {@y2@} &= C \left( {@fx11^3@} \right) \\ {@y2@} &= {@C*fx11^3@}\\ {@y2@} C^2 &= {@num(fx11^3)@} \\ C^2 &= \frac{{@num(fx11^3)@}}{{@y2@} } \\ C^2 &= {@num(fx11^3)/y2@} \\ C &= {@cor_c1@} \quad \text{or} \quad C = {@cor_c2@} \end{aligned} \)

Solve for \(a\) Using \(\displaystyle C = {@cor_c1@}\) and \(\displaystyle C = {@cor_c2@}\)

\(\displaystyle \begin{aligned} \text{For } C = {@cor_c1@}: &\quad {@at(eq1,[C=cor_c1])@} \implies a = {@cor_a1@} \\ \text{For } C = {@cor_c2@}: &\quad {@at(eq1,[C=cor_c2])@} \implies a = {@cor_a2@} \, (\text{Not defined}) \end{aligned} \)

Thus we define the Exponential Functions

\(\displaystyle \begin{aligned} \text{Function 1:} &\quad f(x) = {@ta1@} \\ \text{Function 2:} &\quad f(x) = {@ta2@} \end{aligned} \)
